speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you're experiencing intense itching and red bumps on your thigh and elsewhere; to understand the cause, have these bumps appeared suddenly or gradually, and are they itchy in the center?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies (infestation). The recent travel to Miami, intense pruritus, and the appearance of red bumps are highly suggestive of scabies or a related parasitic infestation, especially given the potential for exposure in a conference setting. I will proceed with a skin scraping examination to confirm the presence of mites, eggs, or fecal pellets. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Scraping_Microscopy.
